ai.definition: Cognitive Digital Twins are full-fidelity virtual replicas that simulate the professional skill sets and decision-making patterns of a human. These twins are created through continuous ingestion of workflow data and behavior mirroring using large language models (LLMs).
ai.howItWorks: Data from an individual's workflows, interactions, and decisions are continuously ingested into a digital twin. This data is then processed by LLMs to mirror the individual's behaviors and decision-making patterns in a virtual environment.
ai.problemSolved: Predictive workforce planning and personalized training by understanding and simulating complex human behaviors and skill sets.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves setting up data ingestion pipelines, selecting appropriate LLM architectures, and ensuring secure data handling. This is followed by continuous data collection and model training to maintain the accuracy of the digital twin.
ai.buildProcess: Data preprocessing, model training with LLMs, integration of real-time data streams, and regular validation through human feedback loops are key steps in building cognitive digital twins.
ai.costDrivers: High computational resources for LLMs, continuous data collection, and maintenance costs. The cost is driven by the complexity of the workflows being modeled and the accuracy required.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Gaining traction in pilot projects and early adopter scenarios; expected to enter mainstream adoption within a few years.
ai.regulation: Current regulatory frameworks are evolving, but there is an increasing focus on data privacy, security, and bias mitigation. Compliance with these regulations will be crucial for widespread adoption.
ai.risks: Data privacy concerns, potential biases in LLMs, and the risk of over-reliance on digital twins leading to reduced human oversight.
ai.profitability: Potential for high profitability through subscription models, data analytics services, and targeted training programs. However, initial investment costs are significant.
ai.futureDevelopment: Enhanced integration with other AI technologies like robotics and IoT, improved scalability of LLMs, and greater emphasis on ethical considerations in model development.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking and high-performance computing requirements.

glossary.def: A type of AI model that can understand and generate human-like language, used in cognitive digital twins to mirror behavior.
The process of collecting, processing, and delivering data from various sources into a system for analysis and modeling.

subsystems.name: Knowledge base and retrieval
subsystems.role: stores and indexes the person's professional documents, communications, and past decisions for quick search.

subsystems.name: Base language model
subsystems.role: provides general language understanding, reasoning, and generation capabilities.

subsystems.name: Personalization layer
subsystems.role: adapts the model to the individual's writing style, vocabulary, and decision patterns.

subsystems.name: Memory and context manager
subsystems.role: maintains conversation history and long-term memory of decisions for continuity.

subsystems.name: Interaction interface
subsystems.role: allows users to query the twin and receive responses in text, voice, or via API.

subsystems.name: Governance and security
subsystems.role: ensures privacy, access control, and alignment with professional standards.

buildSteps.title: Collect professional data
buildSteps.detail: Gather the individual's emails, reports, memos, meeting transcripts, and decision logs, with consent and legal compliance.

buildSteps.title: Prepare and structure data
buildSteps.detail: Clean, anonymize where needed, and organize the data into a knowledge base. Create question-answer pairs or decision scenarios for fine-tuning.

buildSteps.title: Build retrieval index
buildSteps.detail: Convert documents into embeddings and store them in a vector database so the system can retrieve relevant context on demand.

buildSteps.title: Fine-tune the base model
buildSteps.detail: Use supervised fine-tuning on the individual's writing and decision outcomes. Optionally apply reinforcement learning from human feedback to align with professional judgment.

buildSteps.title: Integrate retrieval and model
buildSteps.detail: Combine the fine-tuned model with the retrieval system so responses are grounded in the person's specific knowledge and past cases.

buildSteps.title: Add memory mechanisms
buildSteps.detail: Implement session and long-term memory so the twin remembers past interactions and can update its knowledge base over time.

buildSteps.title: Validate against real decisions
buildSteps.detail: Test the twin on held-out decisions the person made. Measure agreement, identify failure modes, and iterate on data and fine-tuning.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Release to a limited set of users, monitor for errors and drift, and continuously update with new data and user feedback.

prerequisites.why: provide the core language and reasoning ability needed to mimic professional communication.
lets the model access specific, up-to-date professional knowledge instead of relying only on training data.
makes it practical to personalize a large model on the limited data one person generates.
a professional's records are often scattered across systems and restricted by privacy rules.
there is no standard way to measure whether an AI truly replicates a person's decision-making quality.
handling sensitive professional data safely requires techniques like federated learning or differential privacy.

pathway.milestone: AI assistants that summarize documents and draft routine communications using retrieval-augmented generation
pathway.unlocks: time savings and familiarity with AI in professional settings.

pathway.milestone: Domain-specific decision-support tools fine-tuned on an individual's past work, with human oversight
pathway.unlocks: personalized advice for routine decisions and early experience with digital-twin workflows.

pathway.milestone: Interactive digital twins for specific roles that autonomously handle bounded tasks and escalate complex ones
pathway.unlocks: partial delegation of professional workload under clear limits.

pathway.milestone: Full-fidelity cognitive digital twins that act as independent professional agents
pathway.unlocks: scalable expertise, but only after solving validation, liability, and privacy challenges.
